summary: An excerpt from a novel ("Book 14 — part 21") in which the narrator discusses Wilson and his squatting friends, who occupied a foreclosed house. Their group, once a loose family of laid-back kids, changed after an informant named Zip moved in, and the conversation turns to possible illegal drugs and guns the police might find, plus the legal risk of terrorism and property charges. The narrator describes Wilson's protest activity as mostly for fun and the group's rejection of conventional society.
one_line: A fiction excerpt where the narrator discusses Wilson's squatting group, an informant named Zip, and the legal risks they face after police raid their foreclosed house.
key_facts: Wilson was at a protest at US Bank in the Winter of 2012.
Wilson had previously been at Loring Park when police took the Occupy encampment there down.
Wilson was beaten up by the cops and had a lump on his head "like a grapefruit."
Wilson and his friends began occupying a foreclosed house that nobody came to kick them out of.
The narrator guesses the house got tied up in bundled mortgage schemes and the paperwork got lost.
The narrator warns that even if the terrorism charge goes away, the group could be charged with property crimes.
Before Zip showed up, the house was full of laid-back kids who made their own rules and did not bother anybody.
Wilson met Zip at a protest and invited him to crash at their place, after which everything changed.
The narrator says Wilson mostly went to demonstrations "for the lulz" rather than out of real anger.
The group did not go to school, get jobs, pay bills, or hold credit cards or car loans.
The group went dumpster diving for food that was going to waste.
The narrator admits he cannot be sure whether the group had guns, since it has been a while since he talked to Wilson.
The woman asks what the group did for heat, and the narrator begins to feel as if he was narrating.
